title: Trials of lipid-lowering therapy in secondary prevention of coronary heart disease.
abstract: The Scandinavian Simvastatin Survival Study showed that a 35% decrease in LDL-cholesterol was accompanied by a 42% reduction in coronary mortality. Even if the period of time is longer than 1 year for the divergence of survival curves in the simvastatin and placebo groups there are reasons to believe that the beneficial effect of lipid lowering is rapid. The effect may be mediated by stabilization of lipid-rich coronary lesions or by effects on endothelium. Lipid-lowering studies in the acute stage of coronary heart disease are suggested.
